intro: Returning, exchanging and asking about the warranty, discounts, fabrics and online orders.

palabras.consejo: The accent splits i-a: ga-ran-TÍ-a. You ask: «¿tiene garantía?».
It changes o to ue: «devuelvo». The participle is irregular: «devuelto».
It is said about a product: «está de oferta». The offer lasts a short time.
It comes from «descontar». You say «un descuento del veinte por ciento».
It comes from English «ticket», but it is written «tique». The plural is «tiques».
With another sense, «la vuelta» is coming back. With money: «aquí tiene la vuelta».
It is said in shops and supermarkets: «pase por caja». The j sounds h: KA-ha.
It comes from Arabic. The stress is at the end and has an accent: al-go-DÓN.
A wool jumper keeps you very warm. It is feminine: «la lana».
It is always plural: «de rayas». The y sounds as in «yo».
It is always plural: «de cuadros». It comes from «cuadro», a square.
It agrees: «camisa lisa», «pantalón liso». It also means smooth and without wrinkles.
It comes from «caducar». You should not eat an expired yogurt.
It comes from «pedir». «Hacer un pedido» means ordering products.
The ch sounds as in «chocolate» and the qu sounds k: cha-KE-ta. It is feminine.
Past form of «pedir» for «yo». The accent shows the stress: pe-DÍ.
Feminine of «liso». It agrees with «camisa» or «chaqueta».
It is written in lowercase in Spanish: «internet». «Por internet» means online.
Participle of «llegar». The ll sounds y: ye-GA-do. With «haber» it does not change.
Subjunctive of «cambiar» for «nosotros», after «quiere que». «Cambiar por» means to exchange for.
Subjunctive of «devolver», after «prefiero que»: «que me devuelvan el dinero».
Form of «devolver» for «ellos». In «le devuelven el dinero» the subject is understood.
Feminine plural of «ese». It goes before the noun: «esas camisas».
The y sounds as in «yo» and the stress is at the end: yo-GUR. The plural is «yogures».
It comes from the verb «tintinear». The «eo» are two syllables: tin-ti-NE-o.
The singular is «la campanilla», from «campana». The ll sounds y: kam-pa-NI-yas.
The ch sounds as in «chocolate». The singular is «la percha».
The j sounds h. The plural of «jersey» is «jerséis», with an accent: her-SEIS.
The singular is «la falda». The d is soft: FAL-das.
Plural of «chaqueta». The ch sounds like the ch in «church».
From «anunciar». The ci sounds like th, as in «think».
The cu before e sounds like «kwe». The stress is in the middle.
Plural of «enorme». The stress is on «nor».
The tilde on the í splits «ría» into two syllables.
The ch is soft, like «ch» in «church». Stress the first syllable.
Plural of «fino». Say «FI-nas» with clear i and n.
The j sounds like a soft English h. Stress the last syllable.
Plural of «dibujo». The j sounds like h.

texto:
Before buying you can ask: **¿Tiene garantía?**, **¿Está de oferta?**, **¿Hacen algún descuento?**

Afterwards you can **devolver** a product or exchange it for another. Keep the **tique**: it is the proof of purchase. When you go to the till (**pasar por caja**) they give you the **vuelta**, the money left over.

Clothes are described with **de**: una camisa **de algodón**, un jersey **de lana**. And with the pattern: **de rayas**, **de cuadros** or **lisa**.

Expired food (**caducada**) should no longer be eaten. If you buy online you make a **pedido**.

The material is said with **de**: una camisa **de algodón**, un jersey **de lana**.

The pattern too: una falda **de rayas**, una chaqueta **de cuadros**. And if it has no pattern, it is **lisa** or **liso**.

The adjective agrees with the garment: una camisa lisa · unos pantalones lisos.

With **estar** we talk about the state of the product: el yogur **está caducado**, la camisa **está de oferta**.

To offer a solution: **¿Quiere que se lo cambiemos?** (**que** + subjunctive)

pregunta.texto: You say what material it is made of. What is missing?

opciones.explicacion: That's it! The material is said with «de»: de algodón, de lana.
«En» shows place. The material is said with «de».
«Con» would mean «together with» cotton. For the material you use «de».

pregunta.texto: The yogurt has a past date. What is its state?

opciones.explicacion: Yes! Caducado means with the use-by date passed.
«Liso» means plain or smooth. It does not talk about the date.
«De oferta» is about the price, not about the date.

frase.texto: Quería devolver esta chaqueta de lana

piezas.traduccion: I would like to return this wool jacket

pregunta.texto: You would rather get your money back. Which form is missing?

opciones.explicacion: «Devuelven» is indicative. After «prefiero que» comes the subjunctive.
Well done! «Prefiero que» asks for the subjunctive: que me devuelvan.
Here the subject changes (they), and the infinitive does not work.

pregunta.texto: Write in Spanish: «Does it have a warranty?»
You pay and get the leftover money back. What is it called?

opciones.explicacion: The tique is the paper that proves the purchase, not the money.
The garantía is a promise of repair, not money.
Well done! The vuelta is the money returned to you when you pay.

pregunta.texto: It agrees with «camisa». Which form is missing?

opciones.explicacion: That's it! «Camisa» is feminine singular: lisa.
«Lisas» is plural, and here there is only one shirt.
